content.title: The war in Iran is causing U.S. consumer prices to rise - The Washington Post
content.text: Democracy Dies in DarknessIn this articleBy Rachel LermanAmerican consumers have started to feel their budgets squeezed beyond gas prices from the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran, as energy costs have begun to pressure shipping, transportation, agriculture and airline prices.Get a curated selection of 10 of our best stories in your inbox every weekend.With President Donald Trump on Tuesday announcing a suspension of U.S. attacks on Iran for two weeks, the big question is: When will prices come down?What readers are sayingThe comments express widespread frustration with rising prices for gas, air travel, and strawberries, attributing these increases to President Trump's policies, including his handling of international conflicts and immigration.
